About 181,000 resultsHenry Roth (February 8, 1906 – October 13, 1995) was an American novelist and short story writer, best known for his novel "Call It Sleep," published in 1934. Born in Tysmenitz, Galicia, he moved to the United States in 1908 and lived in various neighborhoods, including the Lower East Side of Manhattan and Harlem. After a brief period of obscurity, his work gained recognition in the late 1950s and 1960s, leading to a revival of interest in his writing. Roth's novel explores the experiences of a young Jewish immigrant in New York City, reflecting the challenges of the Great Depression. He later published a series of works, including "Mercy of a Rude Stream," which continued to explore themes of Jewish identity and immigrant life. Roth passed away in 1995, leaving behind a significant legacy in American literature. Wikipedia

Robert Erskine Childers Biography
Robert Erskine Childers was born on June 25, 1870, in London, England. He was the second son of Robert Caesar Childers, a British Orientalist scholar, and Anna Mary Henrietta Barton. Childers grew up in Co. Wicklow, Ireland, after his parents' deaths. He attended Trinity College, Cambridge, where he studied law and classics. Childers served in the South African War and later became a prominent writer and Irish nationalist. He was involved in the Irish Civil War and was executed by the Irish Free State for his actions in support of the republican cause. His works, including "The Riddle of the Sands," have had a lasting impact on literature and history. Wikipedia
